title: Chemical-accuracy prediction of which molecular crystal will form

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reliable way to start from a molecule’s chemical structure, generate its plausible crystal forms, and calculate their relative thermodynamic stability accurately enough to distinguish closely competing forms. Its intended scope includes flexible pharmaceutical molecules, salts, hydrates, cocrystals and crystals with disorder. Generation and ranking are separate requirements: finding an experimentally observed packing does not establish that its stability has been predicted correctly. Ranking must account for temperature-dependent free energies and disorder, rather than relying only on the energy of an ideal, static lattice.

Scope synthesis: the title’s phrase “which molecular crystal will form” requires a careful boundary. A chemical diagram can initiate a structure search, but predictions involving solvents or multiple components also need specified composition, temperature, pressure and relevant environmental conditions. Even an accurate thermodynamic ranking identifies stable forms and competing candidates; predicting which candidate actually crystallizes, how quickly it appears or whether it can be reached experimentally additionally requires kinetics and preparation history. Here, “chemical accuracy” means resolving the stability differences relevant to the stated application with calibrated uncertainty, rather than assuming a single numerical tolerance guarantees success across all molecular crystals.

significance.text: A broadly reliable method would provide a predictive framework for molecular solid forms, extending the reach of existing crystal structure prediction across difficult chemical classes. The practical challenge is consequential because competing structures can be extremely close in energy: the inspected 2025 study reports that most drug-like molecules its authors examined had many predicted structures within 1.0 kcal/mol, approximately 4.2 kJ/mol, of the calculated global minimum. This observation supports the importance of fine stability distinctions in those examples; it does not establish that every salt, hydrate, cocrystal or disordered system has the same energy landscape.

The direct advance would be prospective identification of plausible forms and overlooked thermodynamic competitors, together with defensible stability orderings under specified conditions. Such predictions could guide experimental searches toward forms that conventional screening misses or accesses only under particular isolation conditions. They could also reveal that an apparently settled solid-form landscape contains a lower-energy competitor. Finding that competitor computationally would not, by itself, predict a late-appearing polymorph’s emergence date, nucleation pathway or experimental accessibility.

Conditional impact synthesis: sufficiently dependable predictions could reduce uncertainty in pharmaceutical solid-form selection and help researchers prioritize experiments before costly development decisions. Property-directed design would be a further capability: receiving a crystal with a specified solubility, permeability, mechanical response or morphology requires property models and a design strategy in addition to structure prediction. Describing this innovation as a general language for molecular solids is an assessment of its potential reach, not an established historical equivalence or a claim that any composition could be solved in minutes.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is consistent generation and calibrated free-energy ranking across the full proposed complexity range. Flexible molecules introduce many conformations as well as possible packings; multicomponent systems add choices involving component ratios, solvent incorporation and intermolecular arrangements. Searches must also extend beyond structures with one molecule in the asymmetric unit, denoted Z′ = 1. The inspected 2025 method demonstrates meaningful progress with flexible drug-like molecules, while identifying more complex structures, salts, hydrates, solvates and cocrystals as challenging extensions. The gap is therefore general reliability across this scope, rather than an absence of pharmaceutical-complexity successes.

Energy ranking remains a distinct scientific barrier even when a search generates the correct forms. Small differences can be comparable to computational errors, and finite-temperature free energies can alter conclusions drawn from static lattice energies. For target XXXI in the inspected 2025 study, the calculated room-temperature free-energy difference between two forms was about 0.4 kcal/mol, approximately 1.7 kJ/mol, within the calculation’s errors; the study therefore could not confidently identify the more stable form. Treatment of disorder components in an example does not establish general predictive control over disordered crystals.

A search can also produce low-energy minima that are never observed, and a minimum need not correspond to a distinct experimentally accessible form. Some candidates may represent overlooked forms, while others may reflect model error, limited accessibility or an inadequate description of finite-temperature behavior. Useful prediction requires uncertainty estimates and manageable candidate lists, not simply an expanding catalogue of minima. Conformational exploration and accurate ranking also carry substantial computational costs. Lower cost and broader validation would strengthen routine use, but the supplied evidence does not establish a universal cost threshold below which crystal structure prediction becomes a practical instrument.

current_state.text: The strongest directly supported molecular result in the supplied review is Zhou and colleagues’ Nature Communications study, published on 5 March 2025. It reports recovery of 137 selected known crystal structures across 66 molecules, with the search primarily focused on Z′ = 1, meaning one molecule in the asymmetric unit. Demonstrated examples include flexible drug-like molecules. The study also reports a blind prediction for the agrochemical flupyradifurone starting from its two-dimensional chemical structure without experimental structural data. These are substantial achievements, but recovery of selected known structures and an individual blind example do not establish prospective reliability across all forms, multicomponent systems or disordered molecular crystals.

The same March 2025 study reports possible previously unobserved low-energy forms, substantial computational demands and cases where ranking uncertainty prevents a confident stability assignment. Extensions to more complex and multicomponent systems, and integration with property-prediction tools, are described as future work. The supplied review examined the article text but did not independently inspect plotted data or supplementary figures. Although supplementary files were retained, one had PDF extraction warnings; their presence should not be treated as independent confirmation of every detailed result.

The reconciled research attributes mixed results to the seventh molecular crystal structure prediction blind test in 2024: comparatively successful generation for a small flexible agrochemical, with fewer successes for more complex systems. It also attributes to the target XXXII analysis a finding that observed forms lay more than 4 kJ/mol above the calculated minimum at both low and ambient temperatures. Neither paper was available for inspection in the supplied review, so these remain reported findings whose exact wording, calculation conditions and scope could not be checked. They should not be confused with the directly supported target XXXI example from the 2025 study.

For small rigid organic molecules, the research attributes to a Faraday Discussions paper dated 14 January 2025 a survey of more than 1,000 compounds that located 99.4% of observed structures and ranked 74% among the most stable within thermal uncertainty. The paper was not available for inspection in the supplied review. Those figures are retained as attributed, unverified results; their dataset composition, scoring definitions and meaning of thermal uncertainty remain unresolved. Limited source access is not evidence that the reported result is false, and the stated small-rigid-molecule scope would remain narrower than the proposed innovation even if the figures were confirmed.

Adjacent inorganic work illustrates both progress and the importance of matching metrics to the task. Merchant and colleagues’ 2023 GNoME paper reports an energy prediction error of 11 meV per atom on relaxed inorganic structures against its computational reference. That metric does not establish experimental free-energy accuracy for molecular polymorphs. The paper reports 736 experimental structure matches, of which 184 corresponded to discoveries since the project began; describing all 736 as subsequent discoveries would overstate the chronology. Inorganic candidate generation and stability screening therefore provide relevant context without demonstrating this molecular breakthrough.

An inorganic generative-model benchmark submitted in September 2026 and revised on 17 October 2026 reports substantial dependence on existing structural prototypes among the methods it evaluated. It is a preprint, and its geometric prediction benchmark does not establish thermodynamic competitiveness or justify a conclusion about every generative method. Its supplied landing-page abstract and revised PDF disagree: the abstract names TCSP 2.0 and reports 68.3% top-1 success, whereas the PDF uses TCSPv3 and 67.8%. Both support the qualitative prototype-dependence conclusion, but their numerical accounts cannot be treated as interchangeable.

The research also attributes to Desiraju’s article, published online on 9 July 2026, a forecast that AI might solve molecular crystal structure prediction within five to ten years. The article was unavailable for inspection in the supplied review, so the wording and intended scope of that forecast remain unverified. Even if confirmed, it would be an opinion about future progress rather than a completed demonstration.

Evidence-boundary synthesis: the supplied materials establish important achievements at their stated dates and document limits relevant to the proposed advance. They contain no substantive freshness search record establishing the entire field’s position as of 1 November 2026. The record therefore does not establish that broad prospective chemical accuracy has been achieved, or conclusively exclude additional advances beyond the reviewed sources.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: conduct an independently scored, prospective blind test spanning flexible, multicomponent and disordered molecular crystals, with chemical structures and necessary environmental inputs supplied but no powder patterns or experimental unit cells. Before prediction, register the target-selection rules, success fraction, structural matching criteria, temperature, pressure, component and solvent conditions, computational budget and uncertainty-calibration procedure. A majority requirement should apply within each complexity class, with its exact threshold specified in advance. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective blind predictions meet preregistered majorities across crystal complexity classes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scoring: assess generation and ranking separately. Report whether subsequently characterized forms were generated, whether measured relative stabilities were reproduced within calibrated uncertainty, how many candidates were returned and how many remained experimentally unconfirmed. Broad uncertainty intervals or very long candidate lists should not automatically count as success. Unobserved candidates should be reported separately from confirmed errors because experimental non-observation alone does not establish nonexistence. Include at least one previously unobserved form predicted prospectively and subsequently characterized experimentally, with the prediction and confirmation conditions documented.
completion_criteria.label: Generation and ranking scored separately with confirmed prospective discovery

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: preserve time-stamped predictions, software and model versions, inputs, computational costs and experimental scoring procedures so independent teams can reproduce the calculations and evaluate new targets. Test uncertainty calibration and performance across held-out chemical classes, rather than only familiar benchmark families. Success confined to rigid molecules or aided by experimental structural constraints would not meet the proposed breadth. Report the demonstrated operating range explicitly: finite tests establish breadth over tested conditions, not literal universality. Prediction of crystallization timing or experimental selection of a chosen metastable form would require additional demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible predictions report held-out calibration, computational costs and operating limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CRX-07, “Predictive experimental selection of a chosen crystal form,” is the closest complementary concept. CRX-03 would identify structures and thermodynamic competitors; CRX-07 concerns obtaining the chosen form experimentally. CRX-13, “A growth rulebook that suppresses defects, twins, and disorder in arbitrary crystals,” addresses control of growth and crystal quality. Accounting for disorder when predicting stability overlaps with that topic, but does not itself suppress disorder during growth. These boundaries are inferred from the supplied titles because full descriptions of the related entries were not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-02, “Chemically complete atomic structures of bulk amorphous solids,” and CRX-04, “Atomic ensembles measured from total X-ray scattering,” overlap with the challenge of describing structural variability and disorder. CRX-03 instead predicts competing molecular crystal forms and their free energies. An ensemble inferred from scattering, or a chemically complete description of an amorphous solid, answers a different structural question and would not by itself establish prospective crystal-form ranking.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-09, “Protonation state as a routine crystallographic observable,” could supply experimental information relevant to distinguishing molecular and salt forms. CRX-05, “Experimental many-electron quantum states of real crystals,” concerns electronic-state measurement, potentially relevant to understanding interactions and testing energy models. CRX-12, “Continuous atomic-resolution crystallography inside working devices and static extreme environments,” concerns observing structures under operating conditions. Such observations could test condition-dependent predictions, while remaining separate capabilities from generating and ranking crystal forms.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-01, “Atomic-resolution imaging of a single non-crystalline molecule before destruction,” CRX-06, “Atomic movies of elementary chemical steps without a photo-trigger,” and CRX-08, “Ab initio atomic structure of matter that exists only once,” concern structural measurements of individual, transient or nonrepeatable specimens and processes. They could inform molecular geometry or transformations, but none of those titles describes the prospective molecular packing and thermodynamic ranking sought here.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-10, “Laboratory sources that do facility-class coherent X-ray crystallography,” concerns measurement infrastructure, while CRX-11, “Diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand,” concerns producing suitable specimens. Both could expand experimental access to structures. Their goals remain distinct from predicting the relative stability of flexible small-molecule, multicomponent and disordered crystal forms.

Inorganic convex-hull screening is adjacent work on candidate stability with different chemical systems and validation targets. GNoME’s computational-energy accuracy and experimental structure matches illustrate progress in that domain without resolving molecular polymorph free energies. Property-directed inverse design is another adjacent capability: the inspected molecular study explicitly anticipates combining structure prediction with solubility, permeability, mechanical-property and morphology tools, supporting the distinction between predicting forms and designing a crystal to deliver a desired property.

change_log.reason: The evidence supports the scientific concept but requires separating thermodynamic prediction from prediction of actual crystallization.

change_log.change: Replaced the implication that a chemical diagram alone specifies every target system with explicit environmental and compositional inputs.
change_log.reason: Solvent-containing and multicomponent forms require conditions beyond molecular connectivity, and actual appearance also depends on kinetics.

change_log.change: Acknowledged demonstrated flexible drug-like-molecule successes and qualified the original rigid-molecule feasibility boundary.
change_log.reason: The inspected 2025 study already demonstrates pharmaceutical-complexity examples; the remaining gap is general reliability across the proposed scope.

change_log.change: Specified the March 2025 result as 137 selected known structures across 66 molecules, primarily within Z′ = 1, and retained its blind agrochemical example.
change_log.reason: These details distinguish substantial demonstrated progress from validation across all crystal forms and complexity classes.

change_log.change: Added the target XXXI free-energy uncertainty example and distinguished it from the unverified target XXXII result.
change_log.reason: The supported approximately 0.4 kcal/mol difference concretely illustrates ranking uncertainty without conflating two targets.

change_log.change: Retained the seventh-blind-test account, target XXXII energy claim, rigid-organic survey percentages and Desiraju forecast as explicitly attributed, unverified material.
change_log.reason: The relevant papers were unavailable to the supplied review. Their absence warrants qualification rather than deletion or a finding that the claims are false.

change_log.change: Corrected GNoME’s experimental-match chronology and identified the reference for its energy error.
change_log.reason: Only 184 of 736 matches were discoveries since project start, and 11 meV per atom measures agreement with computational energies on relaxed inorganic structures.

change_log.change: Qualified the inorganic benchmark as a preprint and preserved its abstract–PDF discrepancy.
change_log.reason: Its qualitative prototype-dependence finding is shared across the supplied versions, but method names and numerical results conflict and its scope is limited.

change_log.change: Replaced universal near-degeneracy and sharp cost-threshold assertions with scoped observations and practical goals.
change_log.reason: The inspected evidence supports closely competing drug-like examples and substantial computational costs, not universal claims across every crystal class.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria with preregistered scoring, uncertainty calibration, candidate-list reporting, independent reproducibility and practical limits.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposal assessable without allowing unlimited candidates or uncertainty to satisfy it, while preserving its status as a proposed demonstration.

change_log.change: Integrated roster relationships and access limitations without merging concepts or treating retained supplementary files as independently inspected evidence.
change_log.reason: Only roster titles were supplied for related entries, and the review did not independently inspect plotted or supplementary figures.

unresolved_issues: The exact seventh-blind-test findings, target XXXII result, and 99.4% and 74% survey figures remain unverified because their source documents were unavailable to the supplied review.
Desiraju’s attributed five-to-ten-year forecast remains unverified in wording and scope and cannot establish a completion date.
The inorganic benchmark’s landing abstract and revised PDF disagree on TCSP version and top-1 success rate; no resolution is supplied.
The empty freshness record leaves field-wide progress as of 1 November 2026 unresolved.
The precise accuracy tolerance, success fractions, candidate-list limits, uncertainty tests and computational budgets for the proposed demonstration still require specification.

Some predicted but unobserved low-energy forms may be overlooked experimentally, inaccessible under tested conditions or computational artifacts; the supplied material does not resolve their individual status.
Detailed numerical and supplementary-figure confirmation of the March 2025 study was outside the supplied review, and one retained supplementary PDF had extraction warnings.

Full descriptions of related roster entries were not supplied, so their detailed boundaries remain provisional. The referenced historical item 2 was also absent, preventing assessment of that analogy.

brief.title: Predicting a molecule’s possible crystal forms
possible: Drug developers could start with a molecule’s chemical structure and predict its possible crystal forms: the different ways its molecules pack together. They could then identify which forms are most stable under specified conditions, including temperature and the surrounding solvent.
why: Different crystal forms can change how a medicine dissolves and behaves during manufacturing. Reliable predictions would help researchers choose forms for development and direct experiments toward alternatives that conventional screening might miss.
An overlooked, more stable form can disrupt an established production process. Identifying such competitors earlier could reduce uncertainty before costly development decisions.

sources.showed: This is a study of a blind test comparing predictions of molecular crystal structures with experimental results.
sources.cited_for: It supports the case that predicting more complex molecular crystals remains difficult.
sources.not_established: It does not establish reliable prediction across flexible molecules, mixed-component crystals and disorder.

sources.showed: This is an analysis of a blind-test target comparing observed crystal forms with calculated stability rankings.
sources.cited_for: It supports treating structure generation and stability ranking as separate challenges.
sources.not_established: It does not establish that calculated stability rankings reliably match observed forms.

sources.who: Researchers studying small rigid organic molecules
sources.showed: This is a survey of crystal structure generation and stability ranking for small rigid organic molecules.
sources.cited_for: It supports progress on the narrower problem of small rigid molecules.
sources.not_established: Success on small rigid molecules would not establish reliability for flexible or mixed-component crystals.

sources.showed: Their method recovered 137 known crystal forms, including forms of flexible drug-like molecules. They also reported a successful blind prediction for an agricultural chemical.
sources.quote: For all the molecules in this large test set, the experimentally known polymorphs are correctly predicted by our method and are ranked among the top candidate structures.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates molecular crystal searches at drug-like complexity and a successful blind prediction.
sources.not_established: Recovering known forms does not establish reliable stability ranking across mixed-component and disordered crystals.

sources.who: Amil Merchant and colleagues at Google DeepMind and Google Research
sources.showed: Their machine learning system screened inorganic crystals for calculated stability. Its predicted structures included 736 matches to independently realized experimental structures.
sources.quote: Of the stable structures, 736 have already been independently experimentally realized.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates large-scale candidate generation and stability screening in inorganic materials.
sources.not_established: Accuracy for inorganic crystals does not establish accurate temperature-dependent stability rankings for molecular crystal forms.

sources.who: Lai Wei, Ying Feng, Rongzhi Dong, Madeline Miklos and Jianjun Hu
sources.showed: In this preprint, the tested crystal-generating models depended substantially on familiar structural templates. Removing related templates from training reduced prediction success for some crystal families.
sources.quote:
Removing the perovskite frameworks that the 1:1:2:6 targets share
then costs EquiCSP five of its eight consensus recoveries on that family.
sources.cited_for: It supports testing whether prediction methods succeed beyond familiar structural families.
sources.not_established: This inorganic structure-matching benchmark does not establish molecular stability accuracy or a limit applying to every generative method.

sources.showed: This is an outlook article forecasting that AI could solve molecular crystal structure prediction.
sources.cited_for: It offers a forecast of future progress.
sources.not_established: A forecast does not demonstrate the capability or establish when it will arrive.

shown: Zhou and colleagues recovered 137 known crystal forms in a selected test set that included flexible drug-like molecules. They also predicted an agricultural chemical’s crystal structure without experimental structural data.

Finding candidate structures has advanced further than confidently ordering their stability. In one case, Zhou’s group could not distinguish the competing forms because their calculated stability difference fell within the calculation’s errors.
missing: Reliable searches must cover flexible molecules, salts, crystals containing water or other molecules, and crystals with irregular molecular arrangements.
Stability rankings must account for temperature and irregular arrangements, with uncertainty estimates that match actual errors.
Predictions must deliver manageable candidate lists and distinguish confirmed discoveries from forms that remain experimentally unobserved.
Independent teams must reproduce broad success on unfamiliar chemical classes at clearly reported computational costs.

milestones.label: Blind predictions succeed across each complexity class
milestones.explanation: An independently scored blind test would have to meet advance-set majority targets within flexible, mixed-component and disordered crystal classes. This would demonstrate breadth without experimental structural clues.

milestones.label: Separate scores and a confirmed new crystal form
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to score structure generation and stability ranking separately, with a prospectively predicted new form confirmed experimentally. This would connect useful predictions to discoveries.

milestones.label: Reproducible predictions with tested uncertainty and operating limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce predictions, test uncertainty on unfamiliar chemical classes, and report costs and operating limits. This would establish where the method can be trusted.

uncertain: Some predicted but unseen forms may be overlooked, difficult to make, or computational errors.
Success thresholds, acceptable uncertainty, candidate-list limits and computational budgets still need precise definitions.
A reliable stability ranking alone cannot determine which form will crystallize, how quickly it will appear or how preparation history affects it.
